quests.instruction: Which word names your chest region, the upper part of your trunk that holds your heart and lungs?
quests.hint: It is protected by your ribs.
quests.explanation: The thorax is the chest region. Your diaphragm separates it from the abdomen below.
quests.funFact: The thorax is a bit wider from side to side than from front to back.

quests.instruction: Which word names the part of the trunk between your chest and your hips, where your stomach and intestines sit?
quests.hint: Your belly button is on it.
quests.explanation: The abdomen is the lower part of the trunk, under the diaphragm. Strong muscles, rather than a cage of bones, hold it in front.
quests.funFact: Doctors imagine the abdomen split into four sections to describe where a tummy ache is.

quests.instruction: Your body has four main regions: head, neck, trunk, and limbs. Which region holds your lungs, stomach, and liver?
quests.hint: It is the main part of your body, between your neck and your legs.
quests.explanation: The trunk, sometimes called the torso, holds most of your organs.
quests.funFact: The word torso comes from an Italian word that once meant a stalk.

quests.instruction: Picture a line down the middle of your body. Your right ear sits on one side of it. Which other part sits on that same side?
quests.hint: Imagine a line from the top of your head to your toes.
quests.explanation: Your body has a left half and a right half. Parts on the same side of the line, like your right ear and right elbow, stay together.
quests.funFact: Your body is roughly symmetrical, with left and right halves that are close to mirror images.

quests.instruction: You stand facing a friend, and your friend raises their right hand. Which of your hands is directly across from it?
quests.hint: Imagine looking at your friend's hand across a table.
quests.explanation: When you face someone, your left and right are reversed compared with theirs, so their right hand is across from your left.
quests.funFact: That is why giving directions to someone who is facing you can be tricky.

quests.instruction: Which half of your brain mostly controls the right side of your body?
quests.hint: Each side of the brain mostly controls the opposite side of the body.
quests.explanation: The nerves cross over, so the left half of the brain controls most of the right side of your body, and the right half controls the left.
quests.funFact: The two halves of the brain are linked by a thick bundle of nerve fibers that lets them share messages.

quests.instruction: Reach one hand behind your upper back and feel for two flat, triangle-shaped bones. What are they?
quests.hint: They are flat and shaped like triangles.
quests.explanation: Shoulder blades are flat bones on the upper back, while the breastbone and kneecaps are on the front.
quests.funFact: Your shoulder blades are held to your body mostly by muscles, not by joints.

quests.instruction: Which small, round bones sit on the front of your knees, not the back?
quests.hint: They are flat, round, and shaped like little shields.
quests.explanation: The kneecaps sit in front of the knee joints, where they protect them. The shoulder blades are on the back, and the collarbones are at the top of the chest.
quests.funFact: A kneecap works like a pulley, helping your thigh muscles straighten your leg more powerfully.

quests.instruction: Imagine the sheet of muscle that separates your chest from your tummy. Which of these organs is on the tummy side of it?
quests.hint: Think about what is in your chest and what is in your tummy.
quests.explanation: The diaphragm separates the chest from the abdomen. The heart and lungs are above it, and the stomach is below it.
quests.funFact: Your liver and stomach sit snugly right under the diaphragm.

quests.instruction: Compare the wrist, the elbow, and the fingertip. Which one is nearest to your trunk?
quests.hint: You pass it before you reach your wrist.
quests.explanation: Going down your arm from the shoulder, you reach the elbow first, then the wrist, then the fingertips.
quests.funFact: Doctors call the part nearer the trunk proximal and the part farther away distal.

quests.instruction: Blood leaves the heart and travels around your body. Which of these is the farthest from the heart?
quests.hint: It is at the very end of your leg.
quests.explanation: The toes are at the tip of the leg, so blood has the longest way to go to reach them.
quests.funFact: Fingers and toes often feel cold first, because they are far from your heart.

quests.instruction: Which pair of bones lies side by side in your forearm?
quests.hint: They run from the elbow to the wrist.
quests.explanation: Your forearm has two bones, the radius and the ulna, and together they let your hand turn.
quests.funFact: The radius is on the thumb side, and the ulna is on the pinky side.

quests.instruction: Which kind of joint lets your head turn left and right, like a swivel at the top of your neck?
quests.hint: Think of a turntable.
quests.explanation: A pivot joint lets one bone rotate around another. The top two bones of your neck form a pivot.
quests.funFact: The top neck bone is named Atlas, after the giant in Greek myth who held up the sky.

quests.instruction: Which kind of joint, like the ones between your skull bones, does not move at all?
quests.hint: Their edges lock together like puzzle pieces.
quests.explanation: Fixed joints hold bones tightly together, so your skull stays strong and protects your brain.
quests.funFact: Skull joints are called sutures, and they zigzag like the edges of jigsaw pieces.

quests.instruction: Joints stay slippery thanks to a liquid inside them, a bit like oil in a hinge. What is it called?
quests.hint: It reduces rubbing between the ends of bones.
quests.explanation: Joint fluid coats the cartilage and helps the bones glide without wearing out.
quests.funFact: The pop you sometimes hear when you crack a knuckle may come from gas bubbles in the joint fluid.

quests.instruction: When you bend your elbow, the biceps squeezes. Which muscle on the back of your upper arm squeezes to straighten it again?
quests.hint: It is the partner of the biceps, on the other side of your arm.
quests.explanation: The triceps and the biceps are partners: when one squeezes, the other relaxes.
quests.funFact: Triceps means three heads, because the muscle has three parts.

quests.instruction: Which big muscles on the front of your thighs straighten your knee when you kick a ball?
quests.hint: They are the largest muscles at the front of your upper legs.
quests.explanation: The quadriceps pull on a tendon over the kneecap to straighten the leg, which is how you kick, jump, and stand up.
quests.funFact: Quadriceps means four heads in Latin, because the muscle has four parts.

quests.instruction: You curl your heel up toward your bottom while standing. Which muscles at the back of your thighs do the pulling?
quests.hint: They are partners of the muscles on the front of your thigh.
quests.explanation: The hamstrings pull the lower leg back and bend the knee, balancing the quadriceps.
quests.funFact: They are called hamstrings because butchers once hung hams by their tendons.

quests.instruction: A doctor needs a scan to see a liver or intestines. Which of these can anyone see just by looking?
quests.hint: You can see it and trim it.
quests.explanation: Fingernails grow from your skin on the outside. The liver and intestines are inside, protected by your trunk.
quests.funFact: A fingernail takes about six months to grow from its base to its tip.

quests.instruction: You can feel your pulse in your neck. Which blood vessels, pushing blood away from the heart, are you feeling?
quests.hint: They feel the push of every heartbeat.
quests.explanation: Each heartbeat pushes blood through the arteries, which makes them pulse. Veins carry blood back more gently.
quests.funFact: Arteries have thick, springy walls, because blood is pushed through them with more force.

quests.instruction: Which clear, dome-shaped window covers the front of your eye?
quests.hint: It lies in front of the colored part and the pupil.
quests.explanation: The cornea lets light in and bends it first, before the lens fine-tunes the focus.
quests.funFact: The cornea has no blood vessels. It gets oxygen from the air and from tears.

quests.instruction: What is the long bone in your upper arm, between your shoulder and your elbow, called?
quests.hint: It is the only bone in your upper arm.
quests.explanation: The humerus is the upper arm bone. Below the elbow, the forearm has two bones.
quests.funFact: The humerus is the subject of a joke, because its name sounds like humorous.

quests.instruction: What are the small, stacked bones of your spine called?
quests.hint: Each one has a hole in the middle for the spinal cord to pass through.
quests.explanation: Vertebrae stack up like a tower, with a channel through the middle that protects the spinal cord.
quests.funFact: The word vertebra comes from a Latin word meaning to turn.

quests.instruction: Which bowl-shaped ring of bones joins the bottom of your spine to your legs?
quests.hint: Your hip bones are part of it.
quests.explanation: The pelvis supports your upper body and gives your leg muscles a strong place to attach.
quests.funFact: The pelvis also cradles and protects organs low in your abdomen, such as the bladder.

quests.instruction: Most people have two of one of these organs, and can live with only one. Which is it?
quests.hint: They are bean-shaped.
quests.explanation: You have two kidneys, but only one heart and one liver.
quests.funFact: A person can live a healthy life with just one kidney.

quests.instruction: Each shoulder has its own bone running sideways beneath the neck. What is this pair of bones called?
quests.hint: One runs toward each shoulder.
quests.explanation: You have two collarbones, one on the left and one on the right, while the spine and breastbone run down the middle.
quests.funFact: The collarbone is one of the first bones in the body to start hardening before birth.

quests.instruction: Draw an imaginary line from the top of your head down to your toes. Which of these lies right along that line?
quests.hint: It runs down the middle of your back.
quests.explanation: The spine sits in the middle, while the lungs and kidneys come in pairs on either side.
quests.funFact: Your body looks mostly symmetrical on the outside, but inside, the liver sits mostly on the right and the stomach mostly on the left.

quests.instruction: Which region connects your head to your trunk and carries the windpipe, food pipe, spinal cord, and many blood vessels?
quests.hint: It is the short bridge that supports your head.
quests.explanation: The neck packs many important pathways into a small space, from the windpipe to the spinal cord.
quests.funFact: At the front of the neck sits the thyroid gland, shaped a bit like a butterfly.

quests.instruction: A doctor presses gently on the left side of your upper tummy, just under your ribs. Which large organ is mostly there?
quests.hint: Food lands there after the food pipe.
quests.explanation: The stomach sits mostly on the left, the liver mostly on the right, and the bladder low in the middle.
quests.funFact: The pancreas sits just behind the stomach and helps with digestion.

quests.instruction: Which fist-sized organ tucked under your left ribs helps filter old blood cells and fight germs?
quests.hint: It sits next to the stomach.
quests.explanation: The spleen cleans the blood and is part of the immune system.
quests.funFact: A person can live without a spleen, though they need to be extra careful about infections.
